name: veterinary_clinic_system_004_fvrcp_kitten_series_check
instruction: Run the feline FVRCP series review for the episode. For every feline patient (species='feline') whose FVRCP status is missing, overdue (due_date < episode date), or due soon (episode date < due_date <= episode date + 30 days), and who does NOT already have any queued vaccination_due reminder of any vaccine type, queue one reminder_queue row with kind='vaccination_due', status='queued', queued_by='frontdesk@pawsclinic.com', vaccine_type='FVRCP', batch_code=<nonce batch_code>, category in {'series start','overdue','due soon'}, message '<PatientName> FVRCP <category> due <YYYY-MM-DD> — book a nurse visit.', and due_date set as follows: missing series => episode date; overdue => the earliest overdue FVRCP due_date; due soon => the earliest due-soon FVRCP due_date. If a feline patient has multiple FVRCP rows, use the earliest due_date in the relevant category. Then push one outbound email communications row per newly queued patient: subject='FVRCP series review <batch_code>', body='<PatientName> FVRCP <category> due <due_date>.', logged_by='system', occurred_at=episode. Then write ops_reports rows with report='fvrcp_series_review', vaccine_type='FVRCP', batch_code, category, and reminder_count (one per category plus an 'ALL' rollup). Finally append one audit_log row with action='FVRCP_SERIES_REVIEW', actor='system', actor_role='system', target_collection='reminder_queue', target_id=<batch_code>, details summarizing counts, and occurred_at=episode. Leave all non-feline patients and all non-FVRCP vaccination rows untouched; preserve seeded reminder_queue, communications, and audit_log rows.
_max_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session (anti-brute-force); this session cannot run against a container
_par_steps_note: measure via live gold run in QC session; placeholder only

success_criteria.summary: Expected set = feline patients with no queued vaccination_due reminder and either (a) no FVRCP record, (b) earliest FVRCP due_date < episode, or (c) earliest FVRCP due_date in (episode, episode+30 days]. For each expected patient, exactly one reminder_queue row and one communications row with correct category and due_date. ops_reports has one row per category plus an ALL rollup, counts matching independent Python and SQL derivations. Exactly one new audit_log row. Seeded rows unchanged; all non-feline and non-FVRCP rows untouched.

checks.collections: all seeded collections outside the declared blast_radius

checks.expect: seeded 4 rows unchanged; one new row per eligible feline with category-specific due_date and message
per-category and total feline FVRCP counts computed by Python and SQL GROUP BY/COUNT and matched to ops_reports

hazards: FVRCP rows for non-feline species (canine, avian, exotic, equine) must be ignored; the verifier will confirm no reminder is created for those patients.
45 feline patients have no FVRCP record at all and must be flagged as 'series start' with due_date = episode date.
The seeded queued vaccination_due reminder for patient 5 (Clementine, feline) excludes her from the new batch even though she lacks an FVRCP record.
A due_date exactly equal to the episode date is neither overdue nor due soon and must not trigger a reminder; same for any due_date > episode + 30.
Several feline patients have multiple FVRCP rows; only the earliest due_date in the relevant category is used, and only one communication is sent per patient.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a tri-state feline vaccine-status classification (missing / overdue / due soon) with owner communication and an audit trail, requiring patient-species and vaccine-type joins plus a half-open date window. No public benchmark combines missing-series detection, category rollups, and idempotent report writeback across these four collections.
